summary: Argentina is in a quieter stretch under President Milei. Monthly inflation fell to 1.7% in August, a 14 month low, but yearly inflation is still 33.5% and private estimates put September near 2%, due out Oct 13. Reserves were about $48.7 billion and the peso sat about 21% below the top of its trading band on Oct 5, and the central bank has been buying dollars. The IMF's third program review is still open after a Sep 21 to 29 mission. Argentine stocks move on inflation prints, reserves and the IMF, and energy names also ride Vaca Muerta shale output and oil prices.
for_you: Argentina is a high risk, high swing market. YPF and VIST ride oil above $100. Keep any trade small, and check the inflation print on Oct 13 first.

summary: Brazil voted on Oct 4 and the result surprised markets. Flavio Bolsonaro took about 47% of valid votes to Lula's about 45%, so the two meet in a runoff on Oct 25. Investors read his lead as a sign of spending cuts and reform, and Brazilian stocks and the real jumped: the Ibovespa rose 7.7% on Oct 5 and hit a new record of 209,067 on Oct 9, with the real near 5.00 per dollar. The central bank cut the Selic to 13.75% on Sep 16, but September inflation came in at 4.58% over 12 months, above the 4.5% ceiling, which limits more cuts. The rally has priced in a Bolsonaro win (prediction markets near 87% to 89% on Oct 10), so a Lula comeback on Oct 25 is the main risk, and a 25% US Section 301 tariff on many Brazilian goods (since Jul 22) still hangs over exporters and the Pix payment system.
for_you: Brazil rallied on a bet that Bolsonaro wins on Oct 25. If you want exposure, NU is the cleanest name (Accumulate on pullback, so wait for a dip). MELI is rated Avoid, so the rally alone is not a reason to buy it. Do not open new Brazil swings or sell puts on these names into the runoff: a Lula win would gap them all down at once. Mark Oct 25 on your calendar.

summary: The US and China extended their October 2025 trade truce in late September 2026, and China delayed its rare earth export ban to Jan 10. Tariffs are still high: about 36.5% on Chinese goods into the US and 31% on US goods into China, per a July 2026 Congressional Research Service report. On Oct 9 China and the EU reached an interim understanding to roughly halve Chinese hybrid car exports to the EU over four years, and China will cut duties on about EUR 4 billion of EU goods; EU leaders still have to approve it. China is also pushing into memory chips: CXMT's fifth generation DRAM platform is in mass production and its world share passed 10%, which hit Micron and Korean chipmakers on Oct 12. Chinese large caps are weak, with the Shanghai 50 at a 14 month low.
for_you: China matters to you mostly through the US names that sell there: AAPL and QCOM (Accumulate on pullback) and NVDA (Buy zone now). The rare earth deadline moved to Jan 10, so the November scare is off for now. A new tariff or export headline can still knock these names 5% in a day, so size swings normally and keep stops in place.

summary: Europe is fighting an energy shock from the Iran war. Euro area inflation was 3.2% in August, with energy prices up 14.3% from a year ago, and markets expect the ECB to keep raising rates from a deposit rate of about 2.50%. Stocks are holding up: the Stoxx 600 rose about 0.4% to 0.6% to near 635 on the morning of Oct 12, led by banks (sector up 1.5%) before earnings season, as oil first eased on Trump's Russia Ukraine 'energy ceasefire' claim. The Oct 9 EU-China understanding to roughly halve Chinese hybrid car imports over four years lifted carmakers and goes to EU leaders this week. High energy hurts chemicals and industry, while oil majors and banks gain.
for_you: Europe is fighting energy driven inflation, so more ECB hikes are likely. European banks (SAN, ING) benefit. ASML is the one European name that matters for your AI themes; watch it around its earnings.

summary: The US-Iran war that began Feb 28, 2026 has left the Strait of Hormuz mostly shut to commercial ships for over seven months, and on Oct 12 Iran called the newest US plan to reopen it 'insufficient'. The war is now inside Saudi Arabia: Houthi strikes on Riyadh's King Khalid airport killed at least 13 on Oct 10 and one more on Oct 11, and Saudi stocks slipped. Brent settled near $104.7 on Oct 9, dipped on a Russia Ukraine truce headline, and was back above $106 on the morning of Oct 12; Goldman raised its December Brent forecast to $90 from $85. Qatar shipped only 18 LNG cargoes in the war's first six months against 509 a year earlier. Most Gulf champions like Aramco are not US listed, so the US trade is through oil producers, US LNG exporters, oil service firms and the KSA ETF.
for_you: This is the biggest outside risk to your whole dashboard. Oil above $100 because of Hormuz feeds US inflation, Fed hikes and market swings. Helped: CVX and LNG exporters. If you hold swings, a big Gulf headline is the most likely reason for a sudden gap down, so always have stops set.

summary: India's central bank raised its repo rate 0.25 point to 5.50% on Oct 7, its first hike since February 2023, and said a cut is off the table for now. Inflation is forecast at 5.2% this fiscal year, pushed up by oil above $100, which India mostly imports. On Oct 12 the rupee rebounded about 1% to near 95.7 to 95.8 per dollar after RBI steps to curb dollar demand in the spot market, but stocks fell for another day as bond yields rose for a fourth session and foreign outflows reached about Rs 3 lakh crore; the Sensex was near 71,900 midday. The February trade deal with the US has stalled, and a 10% US Section 301 tariff has applied to most Indian goods since Jul 24. A weak rupee helps IT exporters like Infosys; higher rates and oil weigh on banks and consumers.
for_you: India just raised rates and the rupee is weak. That helps outsourcers (INFY, WIT) and hurts banks and travel. Nothing here is on your lists; low priority.

summary: The Bank of Japan raised its rate to 1.25% in September, the highest since 1995, and another hike is possible at the Oct 30 meeting. The yen is still weak at about 158 per dollar, near levels where Japan has stepped in before. The Nikkei closed near 69,000 on Oct 9 after three down days on AI worries. A weak yen helps exporters like Toyota and Sony, and higher rates help the big banks.
for_you: A weak yen helps Japanese exporters and higher rates help Japanese banks. These are not on your setup lists. The BOJ meets Oct 30; a surprise hike can jolt US tech for a day or two, so keep that date in mind for open swings.

summary: The peso fell to about 18.4 per dollar on Oct 9, its weakest since November 2025. The trigger was Banxico's Oct 8 minutes, which left the door open to rate cuts from 6.50% and said Mexico need not follow the Fed, so the carry trade that held the peso up is weakening. The USMCA was not renewed in July and moved to annual reviews, so trade rules for cars and factories stay uncertain. A weaker peso cuts the dollar value of Mexican companies' profits but lowers costs for companies that make goods in Mexico and sell in the US.
for_you: A weaker peso and rate cuts help the airport stocks (ASR, PAC) more than consumer names. Nothing here is a setup today. Watch only if you want Mexico exposure.

summary: Korean stocks are sliding. The KOSPI fell 3.65% on Oct 12 to 6,384, its lowest close since Aug 11, after a 2.6% drop on Oct 8, and it is far below its June peak above 9,000. Foreign investors sold for a tenth straight session (2.02 trillion won on Oct 12), led by Samsung and SK Hynix, each down more than 4%, even though Samsung guided to record profit. Local brokers blame rising US borrowing costs; China's CXMT adding memory supply is a second worry. The Bank of Korea raised its rate to 3.0% in August and meets again Oct 22. Samsung and SK Hynix have no regular US listing, so US investors reach this mostly through EWY, Korean bank ADRs and Coupang.
for_you: Korea is a memory chip market. Foreign selling of Samsung and SK hynix is a warning sign for the AI memory trade (MU on the dashboard). No action, just watch whether the selling spreads to MU.

summary: Taiwan's story right now is the AI chip boom. TSMC reported September sales of NT$511.9 billion, up 54.6% from a year ago, and a record third quarter of NT$1.494 trillion, ahead of forecasts. TSMC makes most of the world's leading AI chips, so Nvidia, AMD and Apple depend on factories in Taiwan. The main risk for these stocks is any China-Taiwan tension or a US tariff on chips, not local politics. No major new tension was found this week.
